label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents a psychologically resilient group characterized by notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging only 0.81, PHQ-9 depression scores at 0.31, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near floor at 0.04, these respondents demonstrate consistently strong mental well-being across all three measured dimensions. The profile is grounded in a sample of 128 respondents from the training split.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen time or internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness levels (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.81), suggesting strong social connectedness
Minimal depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.31), well below clinical thresholds
Near-absent anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.04), indicating high emotional stability
Moderate and controlled screen time (1–3 hours), suggesting balanced digital habits
Higher educational attainment, which may serve as a protective factor for mental health

label: High-Distress Heavy-Use Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily on social media and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Across all three distress dimensions, their scores are notably high: loneliness (UCLA-8 mean 1.62), depression (PHQ-9 mean 1.65), and especially anxiety (GAD-7 mean 2.06). The combination of extensive screen time and graduate-level education suggests a population that may be digitally immersed for both professional and personal reasons, yet experiences substantial psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, more than 5 hours of daily social media use
behavior_markers: Heavy social media usage exceeding 5 hours per day
Elevated loneliness scores suggesting perceived social isolation despite digital connectivity
Moderate-to-high depressive symptomatology indicating persistent low mood and functional impact
Highest anxiety levels among profiles, with GAD-7 mean above 2.0, pointing to frequent worry and tension
Potential reliance on digital platforms as a coping or social-connection mechanism that may not alleviate distress

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents a psychologically resilient group characterized by low loneliness, minimal depressive symptoms, and low anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.25, a PHQ-9 depression mean of 0.81, and a GAD-7 anxiety mean of 0.80, respondents in this cluster consistently score well below clinical thresholds across all three mental health dimensions, suggesting strong emotional well-being and social connectedness.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily internet/screen use
behavior_markers: Reports very low levels of loneliness, indicating robust social connections
Exhibits minimal depressive symptoms, suggesting stable mood and daily functioning
Displays low anxiety levels, consistent with effective stress management
Maintains moderate internet/screen use (1–3 hours), avoiding excessive digital engagement
Holds advanced educational attainment, which may correlate with greater access to coping resources
